absent: Reference counting and lifetime rules for seccomp filters beyond acquisition and release pairing.
Permission and attach validation performed by ptrace attach and check helpers and architecture handlers.
Signal-specific code tables, full siginfo layout definitions, and user extension sizing.
Notifier chain ordering, priority semantics, and return-code handling beyond registration.
Machine layer restart, halt, and power-off behavior and reboot CPU selection.
Device resource management, syscore shutdown sequencing, and usermode helper disabling.
Range array ownership, initial contents, and capacity chosen by real callers.
Log formatting, dump collection, and flush behavior.
Compatibility pointer translation and 32-bit time field conversion details beyond the shown branches.
System state transitions outside restart, halt, and power-off.

findings.text: Privileged query for seccomp filter metadata of another task. It requires administrative privilege and requires the caller to have filtering disabled, clamps the caller size, reads a filter offset from user memory, resolves that filter, reflects logging enablement in returned flags, copies the record back to user memory, and reports transferred size or a negative failure.

Native siginfo import from user memory into kernel storage. It copies a fixed kernel representation and then validates any trailing extension, succeeding only when both the copy and the extension check succeed.

Compatibility siginfo import that fetches a 32-bit user representation and normalizes it into native kernel storage by clearing the destination and translating the common header plus the payload appropriate to the computed layout, widening compact address-like fields.

Native ptrace system entry handling self tracing directly, resolving other targets by numeric identifier, routing attach style requests to an attach path, and routing remaining requests through attach validation followed by an architecture handler with conditional thaw of the traced task.

Compatibility ptrace system entry and request dispatcher. The entry mirrors native dispatch with a compatibility architecture handler. The dispatcher serves memory peek and poke, event message retrieval, signal information get and set, and register set access where available, delegating other operations to the generic handler.

Range set helpers over a caller array with capacity and live count. They support appending an interval, appending with coalescing of overlapping or touching intervals, removing an interval with trimming or splitting, compacting empty slots, and ordering live entries by start.
Registration lifecycle for reboot notifications with plain and device-managed forms. Device-managed registration ties removal to device release and warns if removal reports failure.

Registration lifecycle for restart handlers through an atomic chain, plus a kernel restart trigger that notifies that chain with the configured reboot mode and optional command and a preparation helper that notifies a preparation chain.

Unified shutdown and restart handler framework with plain, device-managed, and platform-specialized registration. Modes select power-off preparation, power-off, restart preparation, or restart, with preparations using a blocking chain and the others an atomic chain. Device-managed forms bind lifetime to a device and platform power-off tracks one active handler.

System-wide transition operations for emergency restart, restart, halt, and power-off, with preparation helpers and a query for power-off availability. Emergency restart records a diagnostic dump, marks restarting state, and invokes the machine layer. Other transitions coordinate notifications, state marking, helper disabling, device and core shutdown, announcement, dumping, and the final machine action.

Filter offset zero denotes the oldest filter in the chain anchored at the task head, with larger offsets moving toward newer filters. An offset beyond the chain length yields a not-found failure, and an internal inconsistency between expected position and resolved entry is also treated as not-found.
Metadata query requires the target to be in filtering mode and the caller to be in disabled mode with administrative privilege. Violations fail before any filter is resolved.

Metadata size is clamped down to the kernel record size and must at least cover the offset field. Smaller sizes are rejected, user copy faults are reported as access failures, and otherwise the clamped size is returned.

A signal code has a known layout when it is the kernel marker, when it lies at or above the de-thread threshold, when it equals the asynchronous netlink marker, or when it exceeds the user marker and falls within either a signal-specific limit or a generic poll limit depending on whether the signal has specific codes.

When the signal number and code pair lacks a known layout, import requires the user extension area beyond the fixed representation to consist entirely of zero bytes. Non-zero bytes cause a too-big failure and copy faults cause an access failure.

Compatibility normalization starts from a cleared native record, copies signal, error, and code, then copies only payload fields appropriate to the computed layout, widening compact address-like fields to native pointers and handling child time fields with a special variant on one architecture where configured.

Empty or inverted intervals never mutate range state. Plain appends leave state unchanged when full. Merging coalesces stored intervals that overlap or touch the new interval and compacts the array. Subtraction clears fully covered entries, shortens partially overlapped edges, and splits straddled entries when a spare slot exists. Compaction moves live entries forward, recounts them, and orders them by start.

Each shutdown mode maps to a dedicated handler list and blocking character. Power-off preparation and restart preparation use blocking lists while power-off and restart use atomic lists. Unknown modes clean up and fail. Default priority uses plain chain registration while other priorities require unique priority registration.

Platform priority reuses one static handler object and reports busy if already in use, while other priorities allocate a fresh zeroed object with atomic allocation past running state and normal allocation otherwise, reporting exhaustion on failure. Release clears the static object or frees the dynamic one, and null or error handles are ignored on removal.

Initial reboot configuration enables the attention-key flag and the reboot default, leaves panic mode undefined with hardware protection set to shutdown, selects an ACPI reboot type, and starts with cleared CPU selector, force flag, halt-fallback flag, attention pid, and legacy power hook. The reboot mode variable has a build-dependent default that is hard on one build and unset on another.
Reboot log output carries a common textual prefix identifying the subsystem.

Sampling of target seccomp mode and filter head occurs with the target sighand lock held and interrupts masked, acquiring a reference on the head before release. Later chain counting and indexed selection proceed without the lock on the referenced head, with references released on all paths.
A global system transition mutex object is defined for serializing reboot and shutdown transitions. Acquisition points are not shown in this lane.

Preparation handler lists use a blocking notification path that permits sleeping, while power-off and restart lists use an atomic path. Registration and removal select the matching blocking or atomic primitive based on the mode.

Shutdown handler record holding a notifier block for chain linkage, a callback pointer plus opaque callback data, a mode tag, a blocking flag, an opaque list selector, and an associated device pointer set by device-managed registration.
Range entry carrying a start bound and an end bound where a zero end marks an empty slot. Arrays of entries are managed with explicit capacity and live-count values.

Filter metadata exchange where the caller supplies an offset selecting which filter to describe and receives flag bits including a logging indicator. Only the offset prefix is required on input while the full record bounds the transfer.

Restart moves from general preparation through restart-specific preparation, then pins to the reboot CPU, shuts down syscore, announces with or without a command string, records a shutdown dump, and transfers to the machine restart.

Halt moves from shutdown preparation marked as halted, through CPU pinning and syscore shutdown, then announces either a plain halt or a power-off-unavailable fallback message, records a shutdown dump, and transfers to the machine halt.

Power-off moves from shutdown preparation marked as powered off, through power-off preparation, CPU pinning, syscore shutdown, announcement, log flushing, shutdown dumping, and machine power-off. Shutdown preparation notifies the reboot chain with a halt versus power-off discriminator, marks the new state, disables user helpers, and shuts down devices.

Native and compatibility ptrace dispatch share one shape. Self tracing is handled without lookup, lookup failure yields no-such-process, attach style requests take an attach path, and other requests undergo attach validation with special treatment for termination and interrupt styles before reaching the architecture handler, after which the traced task is thawed unless detachment succeeded cleanly.

Power-off dispatch temporarily registers a legacy power-off adapter when a legacy hook is present, notifies the atomic power-off chain, then removes the temporary adapter, so legacy and unified handlers coexist during the call.

Native and compatibility ptrace system entries return a no-such-process result when the numeric target cannot be resolved, and otherwise return the outcome of the selected attach, validation, or handler path while releasing the target reference.

Compatibility register-set access validates the user vector descriptor and its base and length fields before invoking the register-set handler, and on success writes back the updated length. Invalid user memory fails as a fault.
Filter head sampling assumes the caller is the tracer of the target. For non-tracer callers additional sighand protection would be needed to make the mode and head observation safe.

Range removal that punches a hole in the middle of a stored interval needs an empty slot for the second half. When none exists an error is logged and the trailing portion is lost while the leading portion is still truncated. Appends that exceed capacity or carry empty bounds leave state unchanged without an explicit error, so callers must compare counts.

Removal of reboot and shutdown handlers warns when underlying chain removal reports failure, device-managed reboot removal surfaces that warning at release time, and platform power-off removal only clears the tracked handler when the stored callback matches the argument.

Negative results encode distinct failures including invalid argument for wrong modes or sizes or unknown shutdown modes, not-found for offsets past the end or inconsistent positions, denied access for missing privilege or disallowed caller mode, fault for user copy failures, too-big for non-zero unknown tails, exhausted memory for allocation failures, transfer errors for short ptrace memory operations, missing process for unresolvable targets, and busy for duplicate platform use.

Mode and state markers distinguish seccomp filtering versus disabled operation with a logging flag in metadata, reboot modes including hard and undefined, reboot type including ACPI, system states including running and restarting and halted and powered off, reboot notifications for halt versus power-off, shutdown modes for power-off and restart plus their preparations, and handler priorities including default and platform.

Request and layout markers include ptrace operations for tracing self and attaching and seizing and terminating and interrupting and detaching and peeking and poking text and data and retrieving event messages and signal information and accessing register sets, signal markers for kernel and user and de-thread and async netlink and poll limits plus per-layout tags for kill and timer and poll and fault variants and child and real-time and system payloads, and memory and notifier markers for forced and write access and kernel versus atomic allocation and done notification with diagnostic dump levels.
